NextItNet’s foundation is stacked causal dilated convolutions with residual blocks, expanding receptive fields to capture longer dependencies without pooling. The search did not establish a directly matching 2024–2026 NextItNet variant with learned gates over dilation scales. Related work supports individual ingredients: AFMN combines multiscale convolutions with frequency-aware attention for sequential recommendation; 2026 FAAM-SR uses frequency-aware gating to balance repetitive behavior and exploratory interests. These provide motivation, but do not demonstrate that gated dilation scales improve NextItNet. [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf), [AFMN](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asoc.2022.109349), [FAAM-SR](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2026.123580).

A relevant cross-domain architectural precedent is CVPR 2024’s Frequency-Adaptive Dilated Convolution, which adapts dilation and frequency selection for semantic segmentation; its results do not establish recommendation gains. An inferred experiment is to retain NextItNet residual blocks while introducing parallel causal convolution scales, such as dilations 1/2/4, and jointly learned, position-dependent softmax gates conditioned only on available history. Small receptive fields could emphasize recent intent while larger fields retain older context. Keep all branches inside one jointly trained network and checkpoint per category, mask padding, and read the final nonpadding position. Compare against fixed-scale and uniformly weighted variants using the pinned macro validation HR@10; stale-interest suppression remains a hypothesis requiring measurement. [FADC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05369).
